# STM32H743 Nano FC + 80 A 4-in-1 ESC: Loss Model, Thermal Model, DShot Timer Allocation, and Netlists

## 0. Architecture and Assumptions

**Partitioning.** In a 4-in-1 stack, the 48 kHz motor PWM is generated by the ESC's own MCUs (AM32/BLHeli_32 on STM32G071 or AT32F421 class parts), not by the H743. The H743 running ArduPilot only:

- sends bidirectional DShot600 to the ESC,
- captures eRPM telemetry,
- reads current and voltage sense lines.

The model below treats these as two subsystems joined by a defined interface.

**Baseline assumptions.** The datasheet values are representative. Replace them with the actual part values before release.

| Parameter | Symbol | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Bus voltage (6S, full charge) | V_bus | 25.2 V |
| Burst phase current per motor | I_pk | 80 A, for ≤ 5 s |
| PWM frequency (complementary, sync-rect) | f_sw | 48 kHz |
| MOSFET class | — | 40 V, PDFN 5×6 or 3.3×3.3 |
| R_DS(on) at 25 °C, V_GS = 10 V | R_DS25 | 0.75 mΩ |
| R_DS(on) temperature coefficient | k_T | ≈ 1.5× at T_j = 110 °C → R_hot ≈ 1.1 mΩ |
| Gate-drain charge / total gate charge | Q_gd / Q_g | 15 nC / 80 nC |
| Output capacitance at 25 V | C_oss | 1.5 nF |
| Body-diode forward voltage / recovered charge | V_f / Q_rr | 0.8 V / 50 nC |
| Gate driver source/sink current | I_g | ~1.2 A, giving t_r ≈ t_f ≈ Q_gd/I_g ≈ 12 ns |
| Dead time (per edge) | t_dead | 200 ns |
| Junction-to-case thermal resistance | R_θJC | 1.2 K/W |

**Feasibility caveat.** 80 A per motor on a nano board (20×20 or 25.5×25.5 mm) is a **transient** rating only. The model below shows why: the board is limited by thermal mass, not by steady-state dissipation.

---

## 1. Conduction Loss Model

Under 6-step trapezoidal drive with complementary PWM, two phases carry I_pk during each 60° sector:

- **Phase A (PWM leg):** the high-side FET conducts for duty fraction D. The low-side FET carries the synchronous-rectified freewheel current for (1 − D).
- **Phase B (sink leg):** the low-side FET conducts 100% of the sector.

Total conduction loss for one motor is therefore independent of D:

$$P_{cond} = I^2 R_{hot}\,[D + (1-D) + 1] = 2\,I^2 R_{hot}$$

$$P_{cond} = 2 \times 80^2 \times 1.1\,\text{m}\Omega = \mathbf{14.1\ W\ per\ motor}$$

**Per-FET average.** Each FET is active for 1/3 of the electrical cycle on its own phase, giving:

$$P_{FET,avg} \approx 14.1 / 6 \approx 2.35\ \text{W}$$

The instantaneous peak for a FET that is conducting fully is 80² × 1.1 mΩ = **7.0 W**. This peak sets the ΔT_jc ripple at low eRPM.

**Copper loss.** Add trace and plane loss, typically 0.3–0.5 mΩ per phase path on 2 oz copper:

$$P_{Cu} \approx 2 \times 6400 \times 0.4\,\text{m}\Omega \approx 5.1\ \text{W per motor}$$

This term is not negligible and is usually ignored in vendor ratings.

---

## 2. Switching Loss Model at 48 kHz

Only the PWM leg hard-switches. Sync-rect turn-on of the low-side FET is ZVS after dead time.

| Term | Formula | Value |
|---|---|---|
| V-I overlap | ½·V·I·(t_r + t_f)·f_sw = ½·25.2·80·24 ns·48 k | **1.16 W** |
| Dead-time body-diode conduction | V_f·I·2·t_dead·f_sw = 0.8·80·400 ns·48 k | **1.23 W** |
| Reverse recovery | V·Q_rr·f_sw = 25.2·50 nC·48 k | 0.06 W |
| C_oss discharge | ½·C_oss·V²·f_sw | 0.02 W |
| Gate drive (driver-side, 2 FETs switching) | Q_g·V_GS·f_sw·2 | 0.08 W |
| **Total switching** | | **≈ 2.55 W per motor** |

**Per-motor burst total:**

$$P_{motor} \approx 14.1 + 5.1 + 2.55 \approx \mathbf{21.8\ W}$$

**Four-motor burst total:**

$$P_{total} \approx \mathbf{87\ W}$$

**Sensitivities:**

- Cutting dead time to 100 ns saves about 0.6 W per motor.
- Moving f_sw from 48 kHz to 24 kHz saves about 1.2 W per motor, at the cost of more current ripple and audible noise.

---

## 3. Thermal Model

### 3.1 Junction-to-board (steady-state per FET)

Use the peak-conducting case:

$$\Delta T_{jc} = 7.0\ \text{W} \times 1.2\ \text{K/W} = 8.4\ \text{K}$$

Case-to-board: the via array under the drain pad (≥ 9 vias, 0.3 mm, filled) gives roughly 2–4 K/W, so ΔT ≈ 15–25 K above local copper.

### 3.2 Board bulk (lumped first-order transient)

Typical nano 4-in-1 parameters:

- Mass ≈ 8 g (FR-4 + 6-layer 2 oz Cu + FETs)
- Effective specific heat c_p ≈ 0.6 J/g·K, so thermal capacitance C_th ≈ 4.8 J/K
- Thermal resistance to ambient with prop-wash airflow (~5 m/s): R_θBA ≈ 6 K/W. Still air: ~15 K/W.

Time constant and response:

$$\tau = R_{\theta BA} C_{th} \approx 29\ \text{s}$$

$$\Delta T_{board}(t) = P\,R_{\theta BA}\,(1 - e^{-t/\tau})$$

For P = 87 W:

| Burst time t | ΔT_board |
|---|---|
| 2 s | 35 K |
| 5 s | 82 K |
| Steady state (theoretical) | 522 K, i.e. destructive |

### 3.3 Junction temperature at 5 s burst

Starting from a 40 °C board after a hover pre-heat:

$$T_j \approx 40 + 82 + 20 + 8 \approx \mathbf{150\ °C}$$

This sits at the T_j,max limit of typical 40 V parts.

### 3.4 Conclusions

- The burst rating should be **≤ 3 s at 80 A**.
- Continuous current is about 35–40 A. At that level P drops by (40/80)² on the I² terms, giving roughly 20–25 W total.
- R_hot is itself a function of T_j. Iterate R(T_j) → P → T_j, or simulate with a Foster/Cauer network (junction → case → board → air). The single-pass estimate above is about 5–10% optimistic.

### 3.5 Bus capacitor ripple current

$$I_{rms} \approx I\sqrt{D(1-D)} = 40\ \text{A at } D = 0.5\ \text{per motor}$$

Phases are uncorrelated across motors. Required capacitance:

- Local MLCC bank per motor: ≥ 4 × 10 µF / 50 V X7R, 1210 package.
- Bulk: ≥ 1000 µF low-ESR electrolytic on a short pigtail at the pads.
- Note that MLCCs lose about 60% of rated capacitance under DC bias at 25 V.

## 4. ArduPilot Bidirectional DShot600 on the H743

### 4.1 Timing

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Bit time | 1/600 kHz = 1.667 µs |
| Frame length | 16 bits = 26.7 µs |
| Telemetry reply | GCR at 5/4 × 600 kbps = 750 kbps, 21 bits ≈ 28 µs |
| Reply start | ~30 µs after frame end |
| Full round trip | ≈ 90 µs; fine at the 1–8 kHz loop rate |
